name: Pumpkin Boy
summary: A pumpkin-tinted handheld LCD: exactly four shades, Bayer dithering, crisp outlined mini sprites at 2 world units per pixel.
description: The whole world is drawn with four warm shades - ink brown, rust, pumpkin orange and cream - like a monochrome handheld console with an orange screen tint. Volume, transparency and shadows exist only as ordered dither and checkerboards, every sprite is a tiny text grid with an automatic dark outline, and a faint LCD cell grid plus vignette sits over the upscaled image. The HUD uses the same four colours in double-bordered windows set in Press Start 2P.
bestFor: farming or harvest games with a spooky twist
game jams with a strict palette
avoidFor: games where many enemy types must be told apart by colour

difficulty.why: Tiny sprites are quick to make, but with only 4 colours every new enemy type gets harder to tell apart.

technique.resolution: Low-res buffer at 1 art pixel = 2 world units (180 art px visible vertically), upscaled by an integer factor with imageSmoothingEnabled = false; LCD overlay and HUD drawn at display resolution.
technique.summary: Every sprite and ground chunk is an index grid of palette indices 0..3, written straight into ImageData as one of four 32-bit colours; all shading is ordered 4x4 Bayer dither, checkerboards and patterns, never alpha.
technique.linework: Auto-generated 1 art px (2 world units) 4-neighbour outline in ink #2a1712 around every sprite; the hero additionally gets a second 1 px cream #f6d7a1 halo outline. Ground borders are 1 px rust/pumpkin edges, no strokes or anti-aliasing anywhere.
technique.shading: Four flat bands per form (cream highlight, pumpkin mid, rust shadow, ink core) with 1-row checkerboard transitions between bands; light from the upper left (L = -0.62*nx - 0.78*ny on trees).
technique.lighting: No real lights: lit objects (lanterns, carved pumpkins, lamp posts) swap to a brighter sprite frame and get a dithered pumpkin-orange halo ring; flicker = frame swap driven by two summed sines.
technique.texture: Ground is per-pixel pattern logic: staggered 'v' grass tufts, 4x4 tall-grass motif, furrow rows every 6 px, road speckle; plus 1-bit-ish decal glyphs (flowers, stones, small pumpkins). A faint LCD cell grid (every upscaled pixel) overlays the image.

palette.name: Ink
palette.role: Index 0. Outlines, eyes, cracks, HUD borders and text. Never used on the open ground.

palette.name: Rust
palette.role: Index 1. Shadow band, bodies of dark actors (hero torso, small enemy), checker shadows, furrow edges, tree trunks.

palette.name: Pumpkin
palette.role: Index 2. Mid tone: pumpkin heads, roads, grass tufts, furrows, halos, bar fills (~25% of the screen).

palette.name: Cream
palette.role: Index 3. Screen backplane: open meadow (~60% of the screen), highlights, ghost bodies, HUD window fill.

palette.name: LCD gap
palette.role: Overlay only: 1 display px grid lines at 20% alpha between upscaled art pixels (only when the upscale factor is >= 3).

palette.name: Vignette / bezel
palette.role: Overlay only: ink at 0-16% alpha in a radial vignette, 30% / 24% top and left bezel gradients, 3.5% dark cell edge.

paletteRules: Every pixel of the world, the sprites and the HUD is exactly one of the four shades #2a1712, #7c3a1e, #e0812c, #f6d7a1 - no fifth colour, no alpha blending inside the art buffer.

The only exceptions are display-resolution overlays drawn after upscaling: the LCD cell grid (rgba(250,228,180,0.2) and rgba(42,23,18,0.035)), the ink vignette (0 -> 0.16 alpha) and the recessed bezel gradients.
The ground uses only indices 1-3; ink (0) is reserved for outlines and actor details so actors always pop.
Screen ratio roughly 60% cream, 25% pumpkin, 12% rust, 3% ink.
Transparency, fades, shadows and glows are faked with Bayer 4x4 thresholds or (x+y)&1 checkerboards, never with globalAlpha.
Hit flash = palette inversion (0<->3, 1<->2), not a white overlay.
Colours from other systems (particles, upgrades) are snapped to the nearest of the four shades.

typography.role: All HUD text: clock, HP numbers, level tag, cards, menus; sizes are multiples of 8 px (8 / 16 / 24 / 32).
typography.css: font: 400 32px/36px 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #2a1712; text-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #e0812c; letter-spacing: 0;

typography.role: Damage numbers in the world: 3x5 glyph grid, cream (crit: pumpkin + '!') with ink outline and a rust underline row.

background.summary: A procedural farmland seen from above, baked per 256-unit chunk (128x128 art px) directly into ImageData: warped Voronoi road net, Voronoi patchwork of furrowed pumpkin fields, noise blobs of tall grass, plazas with flagstones, then 1-bit decals.
layers: Cream #f6d7a1 meadow with staggered 'v' grass tufts in pumpkin (6x5 px cells, density 0.06 + 0.5 * macro noise)
Roads: pumpkin fill with rust speckle every 4 px, 12.5 world units half-width (footpaths 7), checkerboard-dithered 1 px fringe
Fields: furrow rows every 6 art px in one of 4 orientations (rows, columns, '/', '\'), rust clods, crisp 1 px border (rust on the bottom edge, pumpkin elsewhere)
Tall grass: 4x4 motif (rows staggered by 2) with a rust bottom edge and a pumpkin top/side edge
Plazas on road junctions: Worley flagstones 6.5 x 4.6 art px with pumpkin joints (graveyards or village squares)
Dithered checker drop shadow on meadow pixels directly below a field or tall-grass edge
Decals stamped from text glyphs: flowers, daisies, stones, pebbles, mini pumpkins, leaves, mushrooms, bones, cracks; field pumpkins snapped onto furrows
Y-sorted props: round autumn trees, dead trees, bushes, rocks, stumps, pumpkins, jack-o-lanterns, scarecrows, fences, graves, lamp posts, signs

characters.summary: Characters are 10-26 px wide text grids (chars '0'-'3' = palette index, '.' = empty), composed from parts (head + body rows), then given an automatic 1 px ink outline. The hero is a 12x14 grid (pumpkin head over rust body) with an extra cream halo outline, giving 16x18 art px = 32x36 world units.
rules: Hero: big pumpkin-orange head with cream carved eyes/mouth over a small rust body; double outline (ink then cream) so it reads on every ground.
Small enemies have a dark rust body with cream belly or eyes; ghosts are cream with ink eyes and a dithered fading tail - silhouettes and value, not hue, separate the types.
Brutes are procedural ellipses with banded dither (rust top, pumpkin middle, cream bottom), a shaded right flank and a rim light on the left.
Every sprite exists as right, left (mirrored) and palette-inverted copies (hit flash).
Feet anchor at the bottom centre; sprites are snapped to whole art pixels when blitted.
Animation is frame swapping only: 2 idle, 4 walk, 4 enemy, 3 ghost frames; a 1 px vertical bob on odd frames.

effects.name: Hit flash
effects.how: Draw the palette-inverted sprite copy (0<->3, 1<->2) while flash > 0.4; plus 3 single-pixel sparks in ink and cream flying out for 0.22 s.

effects.name: Death puff
effects.how: Enemy shows the inverted frame for 0.22 s, then a 4-frame pixel puff (blob unions, cream with pumpkin underside, ink outline; last frame scattered pumpkin dots) plus 8-16 pixel particles in all four shades with gravity.

effects.name: Spawn from the ground
effects.how: Sprite is clipped at the feet and pushed up by its height * outQuad(t); a small puff plays at the feet. Ghosts instead fade in through 3 Bayer dither masks (25 / 50 / 75%).

effects.name: Projectile seeds
effects.how: 4 rotation frames of a tiny outlined seed (cream/pumpkin), with a 2-pixel trail: rust at 2.4 x and pumpkin at 1.2 x the velocity times 16 ms behind.

effects.name: Lantern glow
effects.how: Orbiting lanterns and jack-o-lanterns: a lit and an unlit frame plus a dithered pumpkin halo ring (haloSprite r0 3..5, r1 7..8.5); flicker when sin(t*11)+sin(t*27) > -0.6.

effects.name: Dash afterimage
effects.how: Two ghost copies of the dash frame filled with a pumpkin checkerboard, offset 9 and 18 world units back along the dash direction, plus 3 puffs.

effects.name: Invulnerability blink
effects.how: Classic handheld blink: skip drawing the hero on every other 1/15 s step while invulnerable.

effects.name: Level-up overlay
effects.how: The whole screen is covered with an ink checkerboard (10x10 px conic pattern) over the frozen game; cards are cream windows with blinking ink triangle cursor.

ui.summary: Game-Boy-style windows: cream fill, 4 px ink border, 4 px cream gap, 4 px ink outer ring, square corners. Bars are segmented (12 px on, 4 px cream gap) with a lighter top stripe. All text in Press Start 2P, sizes in multiples of 8, no blur shadows - only a hard 4 px pumpkin offset shadow on big numbers. Hurt state inverts the HP window.

motion: No tweening of position on the art grid: everything snaps to whole art pixels (2 world units).
Hero idle: 2 frames (head drops 1 px) at 2.2 fps; walk: 4 leg frames, frame = floor(anim * 0.9) & 3, 1 px up-bob on odd frames.
Small enemy: 4 frames at anim * 1.1, leaves on the head sway 1 px on frames 1 and 3; brute: 4 stomp frames at anim * 0.6 with alternating legs lifted 2 px and body bob 1 px.
Ghost: 3 tail frames at 6 fps, hovers 3-4 px above its shadow with a 1 px bob at 3 fps.
Pickups blink between 2 frames at 3 fps and hop by sin(pop * PI) * 4 px when spawned.
Damage numbers rise, are 1 px higher in the first 20% of life and blink out at 20 Hz in the last 25%.
Lights flicker by frame swap (lit / unlit), never by alpha; UI blinks use steps(1).
do: Keep every art-buffer pixel on one of the four palette indices; write sprites as text grids.
Auto-outline every sprite with 1 px ink (and give the hero an extra cream halo).
Fake shadows, transparency and glow with Bayer dither or checkerboards locked to the world grid.
Render at 2 world units per pixel into a small buffer and upscale by an integer with smoothing off.
Separate enemy types by silhouette and value (dark rust body vs. cream ghost vs. big banded brute).
Reserve ink for outlines and details - the ground uses only rust, pumpkin and cream.
Use palette inversion for hit flashes and frame swaps for flicker.
Keep the ground busy but low-contrast (mostly cream with pumpkin marks) so ink-outlined actors pop.
dont: No fifth colour, no gradients and no globalAlpha inside the art buffer.
No sub-pixel positions, rotation or scaling of sprites - rotate by switching pre-drawn frames.
No image smoothing when upscaling, no anti-aliased canvas paths in the world.
No ink on large ground areas - it kills the contrast with outlined actors.
No blurred glows or soft drop shadows - halos are dithered rings, shadows are checkered ellipses.
Don't make sprites much bigger than 26 px; detail comes from economy, not resolution.
Don't rely on hue to distinguish factions - there is only one hue.
performance: Very cheap per frame: sprites (all frames, mirrored and inverted copies, shadows, halos, damage numbers) are baked once into small canvases and blitted with drawImage at integer positions. Ground chunks (128x128 art px) are generated per pixel into Uint32 ImageData by a generator that yields every 16 rows; the noise field is sampled on a coarse 4 px grid and bilinearly interpolated. The LCD overlay is rebuilt only on resize. Hot spot: the per-pixel ground generation when the camera moves fast.
